error_reason: The Planner incorrectly assumed acceleration remained positive (constant) after the chute opened, failing to recognize that the sudden increase in upward drag force creates a net force opposite to the velocity, causing acceleration to become negative while velocity remains positive.

hypotheses.rationale: The Planner incorrectly deduced that acceleration remains constant (positive) after the chute opens. While velocity stays positive, the opening of the chute introduces a massive upward drag force, causing the net acceleration to become significantly negative (opposing the downward motion). The Planner failed to re-evaluate the forces or sign of acceleration after the event, incorrectly treating acceleration as invariant instead of recognizing the transition from free-fall to high-drag deceleration.
hypotheses.check: Verify the physical definition of acceleration when air resistance (drag) suddenly increases significantly at terminal velocity transition; confirm that net acceleration becomes negative (upward) while velocity remains positive (downward).

verdict.reason: The Planner incorrectly assumed acceleration remained positive (constant) after the chute opened, failing to recognize that the sudden increase in upward drag force creates a net force opposite to the velocity, causing acceleration to become negative while velocity remains positive.
verdict.guard: After any event that changes net forces (like opening a parachute), the agent must recalculate the direction of acceleration based on the new force balance, rather than assuming it remains constant.
